zh.title: 華航A330-300汰換進度延至2028年　A350擴編、787交機牽動機隊更新
zh.summary: 華航2026年陸續接收3架前四川航空A350-900，增加廣體機運能；但A330-300的主要接替機型仍是規劃24架的波音787。隨787交機延後，華航在8月法說會將A330全數汰除目標調整至2028年。
body: 中華航空近年持續推進廣體客機更新計畫。隨著2026年購置的三架前四川航空Airbus A350-900陸續進入營運，A350機隊運能獲得補強，旅客熟悉的Airbus A330-300何時退役，也再度受到關注。不過，依華航公開的機隊規劃，A330-300的主要接替者是正在等待交付的波音787系列，而新加入的A350則是擴充廣體機隊、增加航線調度彈性的另一項部署。
華航於2023年公布787採購計畫時，就明確指出新世代787將替換A330-300客機。最新機隊規劃包含18架787-9及6架787-10，共24架，定位為中運量廣體機隊主力，負責區域、中長程及部分長程航線。787-9也規劃導入豪華商務艙、豪華經濟艙與經濟艙三艙等產品。由於新機數量大於目前的A330機隊規模，這項計畫同時涉及汰舊換新與未來運能調整，無法簡化為逐架一對一替換。
從華航官網公布的2026年9月30日營運機隊資料來看，當時仍有12架A330-300、17架A350-900；10月22日B-18923再完成加入華航後的首次載客航班，代表前四川航空的三架A350已陸續投入實際調度。A350新成員確實能增加可用廣體機運能，但華航並未公布這三架航機各自直接取代哪一架A330，不能將每架A350交付視為相應A330立即退役。
真正影響A330汰換節奏的是787交機進度。華航在2026年5月法說會仍規劃於2027年全數汰除A330-300，但在8月20日法說會，已將A330及737-800全數汰除的目標調整至2028年。原先年底預計接收5架787-9，也因交機延誤而下修至2架；相應地，A330-300需要繼續承擔航班運能，部分退租時程也須隨新機到位狀況安排。
華航總經理陳漢銘9月對外表示，787交機延誤與客艙座椅碰撞測試及相關認證程序有關，目前仍希望2026年底接收2架787-9，並以2027年交付12架為目標。上述數字屬當時的期望時程，不能視為已確定交付。相較之下，已開始投入服務的A350可提供眼前的運能彈性，讓華航在787尚未到位時仍能因應航線需求。
從航機定位來看，A350-900和787並非完全相同的運能工具。華航原有A350主要服務較長航程或高需求廣體航線，787則規劃作為更新A330後的中運量主力。新加入三架A350可以改善整體機隊調度、間接降低舊機壓力，但A330何時全面退場仍取決於787實際交機、各航線運能需求與租賃安排。以目前公開資訊而言，2028年是華航最近一次法說會提出的汰除目標，而非保證所有A330一定在該年完成退役。

en.title: China Airlines Pushes A330-300 Retirement Target to 2028 as A350 Growth and 787 Delays Reshape Fleet Plans
en.summary: Three ex-Sichuan A350-900s have boosted China Airlines' widebody capacity in 2026, but the planned long-term A330-300 replacement is the 24-strong Boeing 787 fleet. Delivery delays have pushed the airline's A330 retirement target from 2027 to 2028.
body: China Airlines is continuing a major widebody fleet transition. The arrival of three ex-Sichuan Airlines Airbus A350-900 aircraft in 2026 has added capacity, but the aircraft formally designated to succeed the Airbus A330-300 fleet remains the Boeing 787 family. The extra A350s give the airline greater scheduling flexibility while its next-generation 787 program faces delays.

China Airlines explicitly identified the 787 as the replacement for its A330-300s when outlining the Dreamliner program in 2023. The current plan calls for 24 aircraft, comprising 18 787-9s and six 787-10s, to form the core of its medium-capacity widebody operation. The aircraft will support regional, medium-haul and selected long-haul routes. With a 787 orderbook larger than the existing A330 fleet, the program is intended to support capacity and network development as well as retirement of older aircraft.

According to China Airlines' published fleet figures for September 30, 2026, it then operated 12 A330-300s and 17 A350-900s. The third former Sichuan A350, B-18923, entered passenger service with China Airlines on October 22. The A350 additions strengthen the available widebody fleet, but there has been no airline disclosure assigning each newly acquired A350 to the direct retirement of a particular A330.

The retirement timeline has been affected by 787 delivery delays. China Airlines' May 2026 investor presentation anticipated eliminating the A330-300 fleet by 2027; at its August 20 investor conference, management revised the goal for both A330-300s and 737-800s to 2028. The initial target of five 787-9 deliveries during 2026 was also reduced to two, leaving older A330s in service longer than previously envisioned and requiring greater flexibility in aircraft lease returns.

In September, China Airlines President Chen Han-ming said the airline still hoped to receive two 787-9s by the end of 2026 and another 12 in 2027. The delays have involved seat crash-testing and associated certification work. These were management targets rather than confirmed delivery dates, and the A350 capacity already available helps bridge the period before the 787 fleet is fully introduced.

The A350-900 and 787 play different roles in China Airlines' fleet strategy. A350s serve high-demand and longer-haul widebody routes, while 787s are intended to take over the A330's medium-capacity role. The three acquired A350s may ease pressure on the wider fleet, but the final A330 withdrawal will still depend on actual 787 deliveries, operational needs and lease arrangements. The 2028 date is the airline's latest disclosed retirement target, not an unconditional guarantee.
